images.title: The tens cancel
images.purpose: Shows abc and its reverse cba in place value columns: the tens digits match and cancel, leaving 99 times (a − c).
images.composition: A small three column place value table in the centre with two rows, and the result below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, generous empty margins, the main object large and centred. Three columns headed 100, 10 and 1 in grey (#6B7280). Row 1: three square tiles holding a, b and c. Row 2 directly below: three square tiles holding c, b and a. The tiles holding a and c have teal (#0072B2) outlines in both rows. Both b tiles, in the 10 column, are grey and crossed by one straight grey strike line each. Above the table, centred, small: 352 − 253 = 99 in dark text. Below the table, centred and larger: 99 × (a − c) in reddish purple (#CC79A7). Exactly 6 tiles, 2 of them struck; nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Write the number in place value form; the common factor is the rule.
images.description: Shows abc and its reverse cba in place value columns: the tens digits match and cancel, leaving 99 times (a − c).

image_decisions.why: Place value columns make it visible that the middle digit cancels and 99 is the common factor.
